prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the depth map captures the smooth gradient of the open tiled yard from under 1 m at the bottom edge to over 20 m at the background wall, as the camera wearer turns right from a metal rack on the left in frame 1 (~1–2 m away, partly out of view on the left), pitches sharply down toward the floor in frames 3 and 4, and levels out toward the right in frame 5. Bright white regions clearly isolate the stack of egg trays carried within the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m at the bottom center in frame 2 and bottom right in frames 3–4, partly cut off by the frame edges) and show how it occludes the floor and ground trays (~1–2 m below/ahead). On the far right of frames 2, 3, and 5, small upright depth discontinuities (~12–20 m away) distinguish the vertical pole, the wheeled cart, and the two distant people (~1–3 m apart from each other, with the cart and small ground objects within their reach) from the dark horizon behind them, which is harder to separate in the RGB image alone. However, the depth map is unreliable on fine geometry: it merges the thin bars of the frame 1 rack into blotchy surfaces, completely flattens the hundreds of drying trays spread across the ground (~1.5–15 m ahead and to the left/right) into the floor plane, and lacks the resolution to show that the distant people face sideways or downward rather than looking toward the camera wearer.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates only a few discrete foreground and background instances against an otherwise blank black canvas as the camera pans right, tilts down, and pitches back up across the yard. It successfully highlights the tiny silhouettes of the two distant people on the right in frame 2 (~15–20 m away, ~1–2 m apart, one standing and one bent near a pole and cart) and frame 5 (~12–15 m away, ~2–3 m apart with small buckets on the ground within their arm's reach), making their positions much easier to spot than in the low-contrast RGB background. In frame 2, it also segments the carried stack of egg trays within the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m at the bottom center, partly cut off at the bottom edge), clearly marking its occluding boundary above the tiled floor behind it. However, the map is largely unreliable: it mislabels the carried egg trays in frame 2 as a "cow," completely misses those same carried trays at the bottom right in frames 3 and 4, fails to detect the partly cut-off person at the right edge of frame 3, and omits the frame 1 metal rack (~1–2 m left), the frame 2 cart, all trays on the ground (~1–15 m away), and any indication of which way the people face.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, providing no body or hand skeleton detections anywhere in the sequence. It fails because the camera wearer's own hands holding the nearby tray stack (~0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach at the bottom of frames 2–4) remain below the frame edge or occluded behind the trays, while the two other people in the yard (~12–20 m away to the right in frames 2, 3, and 5) are too distant and small in pixel scale for keypoint extraction. Because the pose map is entirely uninformative here, it shows nothing beyond the RGB strip and is completely unreliable at long range or under heavy self-occlusion. All posture and orientation facts must therefore be read from the RGB frames, which show the two distant people (~1–3 m apart near the pole) bending over or standing facing sideways and away—never looking toward the camera wearer—while working with objects within their reach as the wearer walks forward, looks down at the ground in frames 3–4, and looks up again in frame 5.
